ambiguities.axis: scope of 'respectively' in the two-scenario scaling clause
ambiguities.primary: [every original load, every added PV] pair with [(0.45, 0.90), (0.80, 0.20)] -> scenario 1 = load x0.45 / PV x0.80, scenario 2 = load x0.90 / PV x0.20
ambiguities.alternative: the two tuples are the two scenarios, read as (load, PV) -> scenario 1 = load x0.45 / PV x0.90, scenario 2 = load x0.80 / PV x0.20
ambiguities.why_primary: 'respectively' formally pairs two coordinated lists; the only coordinated list in the sentence is 'every original load and every added PV', so each parenthesised pair belongs to one entity and is indexed by scenario
ambiguities.impact: changes the ground truth; both readings are physically sensible
ambiguities.alt_code:
import pandapower as pp
import pandapower.networks as pn

def scenario(load_scale, pv_scale):
    net = pn.create_cigre_network_lv()
    residential = [i for i in net.load.index
                   if str(net.load.name.at[i]).startswith('Load R')]
    for li in residential:
        pp.create_sgen(net, bus=int(net.load.bus.at[li]),
                       p_mw=float(net.load.p_mw.at[li]) * pv_scale, q_mvar=0.0)
    net.load['p_mw'] = net.load['p_mw'] * load_scale
    net.load['q_mvar'] = net.load['q_mvar'] * load_scale
    pp.runpp(net)
    mask = (net.bus['vn_kv'] == 0.4) & net.bus['in_service']
    return float(net.res_bus.vm_pu[mask].max())

print(round(max(scenario(0.45, 0.90), scenario(0.80, 0.20)), 5))
ambiguities.expert_ruling: A05: respectively 语法配对功能裁定主读

ambiguities.axis: which built-in 30-bus case 'the built-in IEEE 30-bus case' denotes
ambiguities.why_primary: (i) the same author's six sibling items map 'IEEE N-bus' to pn.caseN for N = 9, 14, 39, 57, 118, so 30 -> case30; (ii) the query lists 'branch limits' among the enforced OPF constraints, and case_ieee30 carries the MATPOWER 'unlimited' sentinel (max_i_ka = 99999 kA) so it has no effective branch limits, whereas case30 has real ones (<= 0.556 kA); (iii) case_ieee30 has gen setpoints above its own bus voltage limits, so pandapower silently rewrites the bus limits during OPF; (iv) pandapower's own docstring for case30 says 'Returns the required ieee network case30'
ambiguities.alt_code:
import pandapower as pp
import pandapower.networks as pn
net = pn.case_ieee30()
mask = net.load['bus'] == 7 - 1
net.load.loc[mask, 'p_mw'] = net.load.loc[mask, 'p_mw'] * 1.25
net.load.loc[mask, 'q_mvar'] = net.load.loc[mask, 'q_mvar'] * 1.25
pp.runopp(net)
print(round(float(net.res_cost), 6))
ambiguities.expert_ruling: B02: 语料方言一致性 + branch-limit 哨兵矛盾双证裁定 case30

diagnostic_notes.note: pandapower 3.4.0 ships no 69-bus feeder, so the canonical Baran-Wu data are pinned in ieee69_network.py and frozen with the set (an artifact-pinning step the engineer README explicitly requires). The frozen tabulation totals 3801.89 kW / 2694.10 kvar; parts of the literature quote 3802.19 kW / 2694.60 kvar for a near-identical variant (+0.30 kW / +0.50 kvar). The implementation reproduces the standard published base-case check values (loss 224.96 kW, min voltage 0.90919 p.u. at bus label 65).

the query pins the equivalent source voltage to 1.025 p.u. to represent a +2.5% tap boost, while pandapower's CIGRE MV external grid defaults to 1.03 p.u.; the explicit 1.025 is therefore slightly BELOW the built-in default. The instruction is explicit, so it is implemented literally and the question is not touched.

pandapower's case57 base voltage profile already has 40 buses below 0.95 p.u. (min 0.7199 p.u. at bus index 30), so every contingency at lambda = 1.00 violates the stated 0.95-1.05 window and the answer is the query's own 0.00 sentinel. The item is well defined but does not exercise the loadability search. The query's stated count of 62 non-islanding line outages was verified exactly.

pandapower prints 'branch results are in beta mode and might not always be reliable, especially for transformers' when calc_sc is called with branch_results=True. The value is deterministic for the frozen pandapower 3.4.0 and the query explicitly asks for the transformer-side current, so it is used as ground truth.

pandapower's case57 and case118 carry very large line current ratings (16-50 kA), so percentage line loadings are small numbers and the '>100%' overload criterion never binds in B05; B07's reported maximum post-redispatch loading is correspondingly low. This is a property of the frozen built-in data, not of the query.

network_note / expected_quantity from the engineer CSV are kept as record metadata and used when writing reference_code, but are NOT concatenated into natural_language_query: they name the library and version and pin index conventions, which would leak implementation hints into the ranker input (E4 §2.2c). The ranker-visible text is the engineer-approved 'request' column, verbatim.
